extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering (SWE) tasks, constructed via a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories. The dataset is suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale and is accompanied by a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering evaluation. The benchmark subset comprises 294 executable tasks from 169 diverse repositories.
extraction.license: Permissive licenses including MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1, and other manually verified permissive licenses
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A fully automated four-stage pipeline was used to mine verifiable software engineering tasks from GitHub repositories. The stages are: (1) preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories, (2) automated installation instruction configuration using LLM-driven agentless approach with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, (3) execution-based installation verification in containerized environments using TractoAI for distributed execution, and (4) automated instance quality assessment via a fine-tuned LLM.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sourced from GitHub Archive (JSON archives of daily public GitHub events including issues, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata) and GitHub itself (cloned repositories with full commit histories). Approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase lines were downloaded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025. Benchmark subsets include tasks from January 2025 and March-April 2025.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks were grouped by project versions inferred from git tags, normalized to major.minor format. Patches were split into solution patches (non-test file changes) and test patches (test file changes only). Dependency versions were frozen via pip freeze and conda env export after successful setup.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preliminary filtering to select instances where: (1) the issue is from a Python repository with permissive license, (2) the issue is marked as resolved, (3) the PR is merged into the main branch, (4) the PR is not linked to multiple issues, (5) the issue description is longer than 10 characters, (6) the PR introduces/modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files, and (7) changes affect 1 to 15 files. Execution-based validation required at least one test from the test patch to fail before applying solution patch, all initially failing tests to pass after applying solution, and initially passing tests to continue passing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An instruction-following LLM (Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct) was fine-tuned on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict three quality labels for each task: Issue Clarity (whether issue description is sufficient), Task Complexity (estimated effort to solve), and Test Patch Correctness (whether tests accurately verify the fix). Each label is predicted independently using a 75/25 training/validation split on over 3,800 SWE-bench Verified examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: TractoAI (distributed storage and computing platform used for parallel processing); annotation labels generated via fine-tuned Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct model
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For Task Complexity, fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and weighted F1-score of 0.82 (vs 68% baseline). For Test Patch Correctness, achieved 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity, achieved 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76). Detailed precision and recall per class reported in Appendix F.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 automated quality labels per task (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified annotations for quality assessment; also used for installation recipe generation), vLLM inference engine, TractoAI distributed computing platform, buildah for containers
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The SWE-rebench leaderboard is continuously updated with fresh tasks collected using the automated pipeline. Future work includes expanding data coverage and volume, improving task filtering, supporting new programming languages (JavaScript, Java, C++), and keeping the benchmark up-to-date with new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark supports transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, but may also accelerate development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, bringing potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors emphasize that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Tasks are sourced exclusively from GitHub repositories with permissive licenses and primarily from Python projects where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase. The LLM-based quality assessment may contain errors as it cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) Automated task quality assessment may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks; (2) Limited language diversity - the initial release is exclusively Python; (3) LLM-based installation recipe generation was validated on only 18 repositories and may not capture every project's subtleties; (4) Automated log parsing limitations, especially for repositories with custom test frameworks such as Django; (5) Flaky tests with external API calls or floating-point precision issues can cause validation rejections.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training (particularly reinforcement learning-based approaches for SWE agents), Testing/Benchmarking (via SWE-rebench benchmark with 294 tasks), and Fine-tuning LLM-based software engineering agents. Users can filter tasks using LLM-predicted quality labels (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness) for their specific training or evaluation needs.
